rationale:
Split smr_exists_unit_form_gt into five independent, reusable analytic lemmas. Each is extracted from the supplied 9-step proof (steps cited as U1–U9). The parent keeps only U8, building the form, plus the glue. A single unsplit proof would be roughly 400 lines. Split, every piece is a standard self-contained obligation:
- unit_coord_field = U1–U2: coordinates of v in the isometric chart J.
- compact_lusin = U3–U4: σ-compact exhaustion, inner regularity and coordinatewise SimonGMT Lusin.
- ball_tietze = U5.
- small_cutoff = U6–U7: a thickening neighbourhood with a small measure halo, then Urysohn.
- integral_lower_bound = U9.
There are no dependencies between children, so the DAG is trivially acyclic. No child restates the parent or solves another DAG node. The nearby Lusin and cutoff nodes in other branches (lpf_wtc_lusin_compact_pieces, lpf_c1r_lusin_closed, slicing_mb_cutoff, isoperimetric_lattice_face_cutoff) have different types.

Parent assembly, to be used as the parent's proof once the children are accepted:
1. Get N and J from the listed sibling smr_covector_coord_isometry.
2. smr_ufd_unit_coord_field gives u: Borel, ‖u‖ ≤ 1, ‖u‖ = 1 a.e., and v x α = inner ℝ (J α) (u x).
3. G := {x | ‖u x‖ = 1} is Borel and conull, so μ(W ∩ (A ∩ G)) = μ(W ∩ A) by measure_inter_conull.
4. smr_ufd_compact_lusin_set with E := A ∩ G gives a compact C ⊆ W ∩ (A ∩ G) with c < μ C and u continuous on C.
5. smr_ufd_ball_tietze gives a continuous ũ with ‖ũ‖ ≤ 1 and ũ = u on C. Then μ C < ∞, since C is a compact subset of U.
6. smr_ufd_small_cutoff with ε := μ C − c ≠ 0 gives ψ.
7. Set φ := J.symm ∘ (ψ • ũ).
   - φ is continuous by LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional.
   - φ has compact support by HasCompactSupport.smul_right and comp_left (map_zero).
   - tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport ψ ⊆ W.
   - covectorEuclideanNorm (φ x) = ψ x‖ũ x‖ ≤ 1.
8. v x (φ x) = inner ℝ (ψ x • ũ x) (u x) =: g x. Then:
   - g is Borel, via continuous_inner.measurable.comp (… .prodMk hu).
   - |g| ≤ 1.
   - g = 1 on C, because C ⊆ G and ũ = u there.
   - g = 0 off S := support ψ. S is open and μ S ≤ μ(tsupport ψ) < ∞.
   - c + μ(S \ C) < c + ε = μ C.
9. smr_ufd_integral_lower_bound then gives c < ofReal(∫_A v x (φ x) dμ).

This only rearranges U3–U9's d = (μ(C) − c)/3 error bookkeeping into an equivalent form. compact_lusin returns c < μ(C′) directly, and the cutoff uses ε := μ(C′) − c. U4's N = 0 contradiction is handled inside compact_lusin, which takes C = C₀ when N = 0.

subproblems.title: Coordinates of a Borel unit k-vector field in an isometric chart: u(x) = (v(x)(J⁻¹e_i))_i is Borel, ‖u‖ ≤ 1, ‖u‖ = 1 μ-a.e., v(x)(α) = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩
subproblems.statement: Let P, k, N ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, v : ℝ^P → NVector (Eucl P) k and J : Covector (Eucl P) k ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) a linear equivalence with covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖Jα‖ for every k-covector α. Assume |v(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for all x, α; x ↦ v(x)(α) is Borel for every α; and for μ-a.e. x there is α with covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ 1 and v(x)(α) = 1. Then there is a Borel map u : ℝ^P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, ‖u(x)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. x, and v(x)(α) = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩ (real inner product) for all x and α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k) (J : Covector (Eucl P) k ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) k, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖J α‖) → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (α : Covector (Eucl P) k), |v x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) k, Measurable (fun x => v x α)) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ α : Covector (Eucl P) k, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ 1 ∧ v x α = 1) → ∃ u : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), Measurable u ∧ (∀ x, ‖u x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖u x‖ = 1) ∧ ∀ (x : Eucl P) (α : Covector (Eucl P) k), v x α = inner ℝ (J α) (u x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with its Borel σ-algebra; all measures are measures on this σ-algebra. H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N), Euclidean norm ‖·‖ and inner product ⟨a, b⟩ = inner ℝ a b = Σ_i a_i b_i. A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (a continuous alternating k-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ) and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; a k-vector is an element of NVector (Eucl P) k = (Covector (Eucl P) k →L[ℝ] ℝ). Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 1.17 (Lusin) and 4.14 (Riesz), as detailed in the supplied proof of the parent theorem smr_exists_unit_form_gt, whose steps are cited here as U1–U9; this argument is extracted from that proof. This is step U1–U2 of the parent proof.

1. (Definition and measurability.) Define u(x) ∈ H by u(x)_i := v(x)(J⁻¹e_i) for i ∈ Fin N (in Lean, e.g. u x := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => v x (J.symm (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)))). For each i the coordinate x ↦ u(x)_i is Borel by the measurability hypothesis applied to the covector α := J⁻¹e_i. H carries the Borel σ-algebra, which is the product σ-algebra of ℝ^{Fin N} transported along the coordinate map H ≃ (Fin N → ℝ) (Fin N is finite and ℝ is second countable; measurable_pi_iff), so u is Borel (in Lean: WithLp.measurable_toLp composed with measurable_pi_iff of the coordinate functions).
2. (Pairing formula.) Fix x and α and put a := Jα ∈ H, so a = Σ_i a_i e_i. Applying the linear map J⁻¹ gives α = J⁻¹a = Σ_i a_i J⁻¹e_i. Since v(x) is linear, v(x)(α) = Σ_i a_i v(x)(J⁻¹e_i) = Σ_i a_i u(x)_i = ⟨a, u(x)⟩ = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩.
3. (‖u‖ ≤ 1 everywhere.) Fix x and put α := J⁻¹(u(x)), so Jα = u(x). By step 2, v(x)(α) = ⟨u(x), u(x)⟩ = ‖u(x)‖². By the bound on v and the isometry hypothesis, ‖u(x)‖² = v(x)(α) ≤ |v(x)(α)| ≤ |α| = ‖Jα‖ = ‖u(x)‖. If ‖u(x)‖ = 0 then ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1; otherwise divide by ‖u(x)‖ > 0 to get ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1.
4. (‖u‖ = 1 almost everywhere.) Let x be a point of the μ-conull set given by the last hypothesis, with α such that |α| ≤ 1 and v(x)(α) = 1. By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, 1 = v(x)(α) = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩ ≤ ‖Jα‖·‖u(x)‖ = |α|·‖u(x)‖ ≤ ‖u(x)‖ (as ‖u(x)‖ ≥ 0 and |α| ≤ 1). Combined with step 3, ‖u(x)‖ = 1. Hence ‖u(x)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. x.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 1–4, u is Borel, ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, ‖u(x)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. x, and v(x)(α) = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩ for all x, α. ∎

Remark (not needed in the argument): if N = 0 the a.e. hypothesis forces μ = 0, and the proof above covers this case without change.
proof_key_steps: Define u(x)_i := v(x)(J⁻¹e_i); each coordinate is Borel by hypothesis, so u is Borel.
Expand Jα = Σ_i (Jα)_i e_i, apply J⁻¹ and linearity of v(x): v(x)(α) = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩.
With α := J⁻¹u(x): ‖u(x)‖² = v(x)(α) ≤ |α| = ‖u(x)‖, hence ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1.
For a.e. x with a unit witness α: 1 = ⟨Jα, u(x)⟩ ≤ ‖Jα‖‖u(x)‖ ≤ ‖u(x)‖, hence ‖u(x)‖ = 1 a.e.

subproblems.title: Compact Lusin set: a compact C ⊆ W ∩ E with c < μ(C) on which a Borel map u : ℝ^P → ℝ^N is continuous
subproblems.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and u : ℝ^P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) Borel. Let E ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel, W ⊆ U open and c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < μ(W ∩ E). Then there is a compact set C ⊆ W ∩ E with c < μ(C) such that u is continuous on C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (u : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → Measurable u → ∀ E : Set (Eucl P), MeasurableSet E → ∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < μ (W ∩ E) → ∃ C : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact C ∧ C ⊆ W ∩ E ∧ c < μ C ∧ ContinuousOn u C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with its Borel σ-algebra; all measures are measures on this σ-algebra. H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N), Euclidean norm ‖·‖ and inner product ⟨a, b⟩ = inner ℝ a b = Σ_i a_i b_i. Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 1.17 (Lusin) and 4.14 (Riesz), as detailed in the supplied proof of the parent theorem smr_exists_unit_form_gt, whose steps are cited here as U1–U9; this argument is extracted from that proof. This is step U3–U4 of the parent proof (there applied with E := A ∩ {‖u‖ = 1}).

1. (c is finite.) c < μ(W ∩ E) ≤ ∞, so c < ∞.
2. (Compact exhaustion of W.) For j ∈ ℕ put K_j := closedBall(0, j) ∖ thickening(1/(j+1), ℝ^P ∖ W), where thickening(δ, S) = {x : ∃ y ∈ S, dist(x, y) < δ} is open. K_j is closed (a closed ball minus an open set) and bounded, hence compact because ℝ^P is a proper metric space. K_j ⊆ W: a point x ∉ W lies in ℝ^P ∖ W ⊆ thickening(1/(j+1), ℝ^P ∖ W). K_j ⊆ K_{j+1}: closedBall(0, j) ⊆ closedBall(0, j+1) and thickening(1/(j+2), ·) ⊆ thickening(1/(j+1), ·). ⋃_j K_j = W: given x ∈ W, openness gives r > 0 with ball(x, r) ⊆ W; for j ≥ ‖x‖ with 1/(j+1) ≤ r no y ∉ W satisfies dist(x, y) < 1/(j+1), so x ∈ K_j. Each K_j is a compact subset of W ⊆ U, so μ(K_j) < ∞. (Any increasing sequence of compact subsets of W with union W may be used instead, e.g. K_j := F_j ∩ closedBall(0, j) where F_j are the increasing closed sets with union W given by IsOpen.exists_iUnion_isClosed: these are compact, increasing, contained in W, and every x ∈ W lies in F_j and in closedBall(0, j) for all large j.)
3. (A Borel piece of finite measure.) The Borel sets E ∩ K_j increase with union E ∩ W = W ∩ E, so μ(E ∩ K_j) → μ(W ∩ E) by continuity from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop). As c < μ(W ∩ E) there is j with c < μ(E ∩ K_j). Put E′ := E ∩ K_j: it is Borel, E′ ⊆ W ∩ E, and μ(E′) ≤ μ(K_j) < ∞.
4. (Inner regularity.) ℝ^P is a complete separable metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, so every measure on it is inner regular by compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure (Mathlib instance instInnerRegularCompactLTTopOfIsCompletelyPseudoMetrizableSpace, giving InnerRegularCompactLTTop μ). Consequently: (a) for a Borel S with μ(S) < ∞ and r < μ(S) there is a compact K ⊆ S with r < μ(K) (MeasurableSet.exists_lt_isCompact_of_ne_top); (b) for a Borel S with μ(S) < ∞ and δ > 0 there is a compact, hence closed, F ⊆ S with μ(S ∖ F) < δ (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_isClosed_sdiff_lt). Applying (a) to E′ and r := c gives a compact C₀ ⊆ E′ with c < μ(C₀); also μ(C₀) ≤ μ(E′) < ∞.
5. (Lusin's theorem, coordinatewise.) Let δ := μ(C₀) − c ∈ (0, ∞) and choose η ∈ (0, ∞) with N·η < δ (e.g. η := δ/(N+1)). For i ∈ Fin N the coordinate u_i : x ↦ u(x)_i is a Borel real function (u composed with the continuous coordinate projection). Lusin's theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17), whose regularity hypothesis is exactly (b), applied to the Borel set C₀ (μ(C₀) ≠ ∞), the function u_i and ε := η ≠ 0, gives a closed F_i ⊆ C₀ with μ(C₀ ∖ F_i) < η such that u_i is continuous on F_i.
6. (The set C.) Put C := C₀ ∩ ⋂_{i ∈ Fin N} F_i (so C = C₀ if N = 0). C is closed and contained in the compact set C₀, hence compact, and C ⊆ C₀ ⊆ E′ ⊆ W ∩ E. Each u_i is continuous on C ⊆ F_i, and a map into EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) is continuous on a set iff all of its coordinates are (the coordinate map H → (Fin N → ℝ) is a homeomorphism; continuousOn_pi), so u is continuous on C.
7. (Measure of C.) C₀ ∖ C ⊆ ⋃_{i} (C₀ ∖ F_i), so μ(C₀ ∖ C) ≤ Σ_i μ(C₀ ∖ F_i) ≤ N·η < δ. Hence c + δ = μ(C₀) ≤ μ(C) + μ(C₀ ∖ C) < μ(C) + δ, and since δ < ∞ we may cancel δ to get c < μ(C). Thus C is compact, C ⊆ W ∩ E, c < μ(C) and u is continuous on C. ∎

Formalization note (not part of the argument): the inner-regularity instance and Lusin's theorem are not imported by GMT.Ch06.Submission; add `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.RegularityCompacts` and `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin` (checked to compile with the frozen submission).
proof_key_steps: c < ∞; exhaust W by increasing compacts K_j := closedBall(0,j) ∖ thickening(1/(j+1), ℝ^P ∖ W), each of finite measure.
Continuity from below: some E′ := E ∩ K_j has c < μ(E′) < ∞.
Inner regularity by compacts (InnerRegularCompactLTTop on ℝ^P): compact C₀ ⊆ E′ with c < μ(C₀) < ∞.
SimonGMT Lusin on each coordinate u_i over C₀ with error η, N·η < δ := μ(C₀) − c: closed F_i ⊆ C₀.
C := C₀ ∩ ⋂_i F_i is compact, u is continuous on C, μ(C₀ ∖ C) < δ, hence c < μ(C).

subproblems.title: Tietze extension into the closed unit ball of ℝ^N
subproblems.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, C ⊆ ℝ^P closed and u : ℝ^P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) continuous on C with ‖u(x)‖ ≤ 1 for every x ∈ C. Then there is a continuous w : ℝ^P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with ‖w(x)‖ ≤ 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P and w(x) = u(x) for every x ∈ C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (C : Set (Eucl P)) (u : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), IsClosed C → ContinuousOn u C → (∀ x ∈ C, ‖u x‖ ≤ 1) → ∃ w : Eucl P → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), Continuous w ∧ (∀ x, ‖w x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x ∈ C, w x = u x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with its Borel σ-algebra; all measures are measures on this σ-algebra. H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N), Euclidean norm ‖·‖ and inner product ⟨a, b⟩ = inner ℝ a b = Σ_i a_i b_i. Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 1.17 (Lusin) and 4.14 (Riesz), as detailed in the supplied proof of the parent theorem smr_exists_unit_form_gt, whose steps are cited here as U1–U9; this argument is extracted from that proof. This is step U5 of the parent proof.

Let B := closedBall(0, 1) ⊆ H.
1. (Restriction to C.) Since u is continuous on C and u(C) ⊆ B, the map f : C → B, f(x) := u(x), is a continuous map from the subspace C ⊆ ℝ^P to the subspace B ⊆ H.
2. (Tietze extension.) ℝ^P is a metric space, hence normal, and C is closed. The closed unit ball B of the finite-dimensional real normed space H has the Tietze extension property (Mathlib instance Set.instTietzeExtensionUnitClosedBall in Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Tietze, with 𝕜 = ℝ). Hence by ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq there is a continuous g : ℝ^P → B whose restriction to C is f (equivalently, ContinuousMap.exists_forall_mem_restrict_eq applied to f viewed as a map C → H with values in B gives a continuous g : ℝ^P → H with g(x) ∈ B for all x and g = f on C).
(Elementary alternative for step 2: each coordinate x ↦ u(x)_i is a continuous real function on the closed set C, so by the real Tietze extension theorem it extends to a continuous real function on ℝ^P; together these give a continuous F : ℝ^P → H with F = u on C. The radial retraction ρ(y) := y / max(1, ‖y‖) is continuous on H (the denominator is continuous and ≥ 1), satisfies ‖ρ(y)‖ = ‖y‖/max(1, ‖y‖) ≤ 1 and ρ(y) = y when ‖y‖ ≤ 1; so g := ρ ∘ F is continuous with values in B and g = u on C because u(C) ⊆ B.)
3. (Conclusion.) Let w(x) := g(x) ∈ H (composition of g with the continuous inclusion B ⊆ H). Then w is continuous, ‖w(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x because g(x) ∈ B, and for x ∈ C, w(x) = f(x) = u(x). ∎

Formalization note (not part of the argument): add `import Mathlib.Topology.TietzeExtension` and `import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Tietze` (the latter provides TietzeExtension (Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) 1)); checked to compile with the frozen submission.
proof_key_steps: Restrict u to a continuous map f : C → closedBall(0,1).

Tietze for the closed unit ball of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^N (or coordinatewise Tietze followed by the radial retraction y ↦ y/max(1,‖y‖)) gives a continuous extension g : ℝ^P → closedBall(0,1).
w := g viewed in ℝ^N is continuous, ‖w‖ ≤ 1 and w = u on C.

subproblems.title: Urysohn cutoff with small measure halo: ψ = 1 on a compact C, tsupport ψ ⊆ W, μ(support ψ ∖ C) < ε
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let C ⊆ ℝ^P be compact and W ⊆ U open with C ⊆ W, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a continuous ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support, tsupport ψ ⊆ W, 0 ≤ ψ(x) ≤ 1 for all x, ψ = 1 on C, and μ(support ψ ∖ C) < ε.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)), (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → ∀ C W : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact C → IsOpen W → C ⊆ W → W ⊆ U → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, ε ≠ 0 → ∃ ψ : Eucl P → ℝ, Continuous ψ ∧ HasCompactSupport ψ ∧ tsupport ψ ⊆ W ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ψ x ∧ ψ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ C, ψ x = 1) ∧ μ (Function.support ψ \ C) < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with its Borel σ-algebra; all measures are measures on this σ-algebra. Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 1.17 (Lusin) and 4.14 (Riesz), as detailed in the supplied proof of the parent theorem smr_exists_unit_form_gt, whose steps are cited here as U1–U9; this argument is extracted from that proof. This is step U6–U7 of the parent proof.

1. (A compact neighbourhood inside W.) Since C is compact, W is open and C ⊆ W, there is r > 0 with K″ := cthickening(r, C) ⊆ W (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), where cthickening(δ, C) = {x : infEdist(x, C) ≤ δ}. K″ is closed and bounded (C is bounded), hence compact because ℝ^P is proper (or: IsCompact.cthickening). As K″ ⊆ W ⊆ U, μ(K″) < ∞.
2. (Shrinking open neighbourhoods.) For j ∈ ℕ let O_j := thickening(r/(j+1), C) = {x : infEdist(x, C) < r/(j+1)}, an open set. Since r/(j+1) decreases in j, O_{j+1} ⊆ O_j. C ⊆ O_j (points of C have infEdist 0 < r/(j+1)), and O_j ⊆ cthickening(r/(j+1), C) ⊆ cthickening(r, C) = K″. Moreover ⋂_j O_j ⊆ C: if infEdist(x, C) < r/(j+1) for every j then infEdist(x, C) = 0, so x ∈ closure C = C (C is compact, hence closed).
3. (Small halo.) The sets D_j := O_j ∖ C are Borel (open minus closed) and decreasing, μ(D_0) ≤ μ(K″) < ∞, and ⋂_j D_j = (⋂_j O_j) ∖ C = ∅. By continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop) μ(D_j) → μ(∅) = 0. Since ε > 0 there is j with μ(O_j ∖ C) < ε. Fix such a j and put O := O_j.
4. (Urysohn's lemma.) ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, C is compact, ℝ^P ∖ O is closed, and C ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ O) = ∅ because C ⊆ O. By exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact there is a continuous ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ with ψ = 1 on C, ψ = 0 on ℝ^P ∖ O, compact support, and ψ(x) ∈ [0, 1] for all x.
5. (Support.) ψ vanishes off O, so support ψ ⊆ O. Hence tsupport ψ = closure(support ψ) ⊆ closure O ⊆ cthickening(r/(j+1), C) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ K″ ⊆ W, and μ(support ψ ∖ C) ≤ μ(O ∖ C) < ε. Together with step 4, ψ is continuous, has compact support, tsupport ψ ⊆ W, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on C and μ(support ψ ∖ C) < ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose r > 0 with the compact K″ := cthickening(r, C) ⊆ W; μ(K″) < ∞.
O_j := thickening(r/(j+1), C) are open, decreasing, contain C, lie in K″ and ⋂_j O_j = C.
Continuity from above on O_j ∖ C (finite measure, empty intersection): some O := O_j has μ(O ∖ C) < ε.
Urysohn (exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact) for C and ℝ^P ∖ O gives ψ ∈ [0,1], ψ = 1 on C, ψ = 0 off O, compact support.
support ψ ⊆ O, so tsupport ψ ⊆ closure O ⊆ K″ ⊆ W and μ(support ψ ∖ C) ≤ μ(O ∖ C) < ε.

subproblems.title: Lower bound ∫_A g dμ > c for |g| ≤ 1, g = 1 on C ⊆ A, g = 0 off S, c + μ(S ∖ C) < μ(C)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, g : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel with |g(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and A, C, S ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with C ⊆ A and μ(S) < ∞. Assume g = 1 on C, g = 0 off S, and c ∈ [0, ∞] satisfies c + μ(S ∖ C) < μ(C). Then c < ENNReal.ofReal(∫_A g dμ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ) (A C S : Set (Eucl P)) (c : ℝ≥0∞), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet C → MeasurableSet S → C ⊆ A → μ S < ∞ → Measurable g → (∀ x, |g x| ≤ 1) → (∀ x ∈ C, g x = 1) → (∀ x, x ∉ S → g x = 0) → c + μ (S \ C) < μ C → c < ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x in A, g x ∂μ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with its Borel σ-algebra; all measures are measures on this σ-algebra. ∫_A f dμ means ∫ x in A, f x ∂μ (Bochner integral for μ.restrict A). Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (pp. 136–137), with Ch. 1, 1.17 (Lusin) and 4.14 (Riesz), as detailed in the supplied proof of the parent theorem smr_exists_unit_form_gt, whose steps are cited here as U1–U9; this argument is extracted from that proof. This is step U9 of the parent proof.

1. (Finiteness.) C ⊆ S: if x ∈ C ∖ S then 1 = g(x) = 0, which is impossible. Hence μ(C) ≤ μ(S) < ∞, and c + μ(S ∖ C) < μ(C) < ∞ gives c < ∞ and μ(S ∖ C) < ∞. Put a := μ(C).toReal, b := μ(S ∖ C).toReal and c′ := c.toReal ≥ 0. Since toReal is additive and strictly monotone on finite values, c′ + b < a.
2. (Integrability.) For every x, |g(x)| ≤ 1_S(x) (|g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = 0 off S). g is Borel and ∫ 1_S dμ = μ(S) < ∞, so g is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'), and hence integrable on every measurable set, in particular on A, C and A ∖ C.
3. (Splitting.) Since C is Borel and A ∩ C = C (C ⊆ A), ∫_A g dμ = ∫_{A∩C} g dμ + ∫_{A∖C} g dμ = ∫_C g dμ + ∫_{A∖C} g dμ (integral_inter_add_sdiff). As g = 1 on the Borel set C, ∫_C g dμ = ∫_C 1 dμ = μ(C).toReal = a (setIntegral_congr_fun, setIntegral_const).
4. (The remainder is small.) g vanishes on (A ∖ C) ∖ S, so ∫_{A∖C} g dμ = ∫_{(A∖C)∩S} g dμ, and since |g| ≤ 1 and μ((A∖C) ∩ S) ≤ μ(S ∖ C) < ∞, |∫_{(A∖C)∩S} g dμ| ≤ 1·μ((A∖C) ∩ S).toReal ≤ μ(S ∖ C).toReal = b (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const). Equivalently, |∫_{A∖C} g dμ| ≤ ∫_{A∖C} 1_S dμ ≤ b.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–4 and step 1, ∫_A g dμ ≥ a − b > c′ ≥ 0. Since c ≠ ∞, c = ENNReal.ofReal(c′), and since 0 < ∫_A g dμ, ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff gives c = ENNReal.ofReal(c′) < ENNReal.ofReal(∫_A g dμ). ∎
proof_key_steps: C ⊆ S, so μ(C) ≤ μ(S) < ∞; all of c, μ(S∖C), μ(C) are finite and c.toReal + μ(S∖C).toReal < μ(C).toReal.
|g| ≤ 1_S with μ(S) < ∞ makes g integrable.
∫_A g = ∫_C g + ∫_{A∖C} g = μ(C).toReal + ∫_{A∖C} g.
|∫_{A∖C} g| ≤ μ((A∖C) ∩ S).toReal ≤ μ(S∖C).toReal.
∫_A g > c.toReal ≥ 0, hence c < ENNReal.ofReal(∫_A g).
